instruction:
Use the National Archives census guidance to compare the 1890, 1940 and 1950 US population censuses. For each, report the census reference date, whether the population schedules are complete or partly lost, the public release date if stated, and the free official online research route. For 1940 and 1950, follow their question guides to distinguish information requested from everyone from supplemental questions requested from a sample; compare residence, education and income questions, preserving the stated reference periods. Read the general access guidance and the 1950 search help to explain the 72-year restriction, enumeration-district searches, and the limitation of machine-generated name transcription. Produce a three-year comparison and a separate checklist for a researcher who knows a town and street but cannot find a name. Do not search for an actual person, use a paid partner, or order records. Cite the specific official pages supporting each route and limitation.

Stopping condition: Stop when a cited three-census comparison covers dates, preservation, access and requested question differences, followed by the address-without-name research checklist and its limitations.

Constraints:
- Only use the browser actions available to you. Do not open API endpoints, raw data files, view-source pages or downloads, and do not use external programs.
- Do not sign in or create accounts. Do not provide anyone's private personal information; use only task-supplied fictional values if an interaction requests personal details.
- Remain read-only: do not purchase, reserve, apply, post, send messages, contact people or change external records.
- Navigation, search, filtering, sorting and read-only form or calculator interactions are allowed.
- Do not bypass authentication, paywalls, CAPTCHAs or access challenges. Dismiss optional prompts without creating an account or supplying personal information.
- Support the answer with observed page evidence and source URLs. For values that can change, report what the site shows during the run. Preserve the requested dates, units and scope; report unavailable information explicitly instead of inventing it.

items.description: Report the 1890 census reference date, whether the population schedules are complete or partly lost, the public release date if stated, and the free official online research route. Full credit if all elements are accurately retrieved from the National Archives site, explicitly noted if any specific detail is unstated on the source pages, or if the agent clearly reports that the National Archives site is inaccessible/down.

Report the 1940 census reference date, whether the population schedules are complete or partly lost, the public release date if stated, and the free official online research route. Full credit if all elements are accurately retrieved, explicitly noted if any specific detail is unstated, or if the agent clearly reports that the National Archives site is inaccessible.

Report the 1950 census reference date, whether the population schedules are complete or partly lost, the public release date if stated, and the free official online research route. Full credit if all elements are accurately retrieved, explicitly noted if any specific detail is unstated, or if the agent clearly reports that the National Archives site is inaccessible.

Distinguish between questions requested from everyone versus supplemental sample questions for both 1940 and 1950. Compare the residence, education, and income questions between the two years, preserving the stated reference periods. Full credit if the differences and reference periods are clearly detailed based on the official question guides, or if the agent clearly reports that the specific guides or National Archives site were inaccessible.

items.criterion: Explanation of Search Mechanics and Restrictions
items.description: Explain the 72-year restriction (from general access guidance), how enumeration-district searches work, and the limitations of machine-generated name transcription (from the 1950 search help). Full credit for covering all three topics accurately according to the NARA help pages, or if the agent clearly reports that the required pages were inaccessible/blocked.

Produce a three-year comparison section and a separate checklist section specifically designed for a researcher who knows a town and street but cannot find a name. Full credit if both distinct sections/formats are clearly provided. If the site was inaccessible, full credit is awarded if the agent still provides the structural formats containing the unavailability explanations.

Cite the specific official National Archives pages that support each research route and limitation. Adhere to constraints by not searching for an actual person, using a paid partner, or ordering records. Full credit if citations are present (or appropriately omitted if the site was inaccessible and no pages could be viewed) and all negative constraints are respected.
